To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated human iPSCs carrying large-scale mtDNA deletions, which can be used to model mitochondrial disease and study the mechanisms involved in the disease progression.

we generated human induced pluripoent stem cells from two PMPS patient, carrying different type large scale mtDNA deletions, and that the hiPSCs were able to differentiate to the haematopoetic lineage.
we generated hiPSC lines from two different PMPS patients, and characterized them for the presence of the heteroplasmic deletion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of hiPSC lines from PMPS patients, and the characterization of these hiPSCs, including the mtDNA heteroplasmy and its effect on mitochondrial function.

the generation and characterization of two hiPSC lines (FINCBi002-A, FINCBi003A), derived from two PMPS patient fibroblasts carrying different type of heteroplasmic large-scale deletion of mtDNA, which can serve as a valuable model for PMPS and for studying mitochondrial diseases.
the study of PMPS and other mitochondrial diseases by using hiPSCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hiPSCs derived from PMPS patients are suitable for the investigation of the mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of the disease, and may be used to test the efficacy of potential therapeutic approaches, including the replacement of the deleted mtDNA molecules with the normal ones.
the hiPSC lines, FINC-Bi002-A and Bi003-A, are human induced pluripotential stem cell lines, generated from PMPS patients, that carry heteroplasmic large-scale deletion of mitochondrial DNA.
we successfully generated two PMPS hiPSC lines from two PMPS patient-derived fibroblasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PMPS patient-specific hiPSCs, FINCBi003A (carrying a large deletion in the ND5 gene) and FINCBi002A (carrying the large deletion in the COI gene) can be differentiated into functional pancreatic cells, as demonstrated by insulin secretion and the expression of insulin, glucokinase, and Pdx1.

we have established two hiPSC lines, FINC-Bi002-A and -B, and FINCBi002-B, carrying heteroplasic macrodeletion of mtDNA causing Pearson's syndrome, and that these hiPSC lines are valuable models to study mitochondrial diseases and to develop new therapies.
we have generated two PMPS hiPSC lines, FINC Bi002-A and FINC Bi003-A, carrying a 6,000 bp and a 7,200 bp heteroplasmic deletion of mtDNA, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the two hiPSC lines are able to differentiate in all three germ layers, including haematopoietic cells, and that the Δ mtDNA is present in both cell lines in variable proportion, depending on the differentiation stage.
hiPSCs carrying a large-scale deletion of mitochondrial genome can be generated from PMPS patients.

the two hiPSC clones, FINCBi001-A and FINCBI002-A, are heteroplasmic for the large-scale mtDNAs deletion, which is maintained during the differentiation of these hiPSCs to haematopoietic progenitors, as well as to cardiomyocytes and neurons.
